  • Alt + 0216 = Ø (Used for 'kra' - क्र)
  • Alt + 0170 = ª (Used for 'nga' with a dot)
  • Alt + 0167 = § (Used for half 'ta')
  • Alt + 0183 = · (Used for a middle dot)

Unicode Typing Shortcuts

When typing in Nepali Unicode (such as Traditional or Romanized layouts), you rarely need Alt codes because Unicode supports native character combining. Instead, you use the Halant (्) to connect characters.

  • To type क्र (Kra): Type क + ् + र
  • To type श्र (Shra): Type श + ् + र
  • To type क्ष (Ksha): Type क + ् + ष
  • To type त्र (Tra): Type त + ् + र
  • To type ज्ञ (Gya): Type ज + ् + ञ

title: Preeti vs Mangal Font: What is the Difference?
excerpt: A detailed breakdown of the differences between Nepal's most famous legacy font (Preeti) and Microsoft's default Devanagari Unicode font (Mangal).
content:
Understanding the Two Heavyweights

When working with Nepali text on a computer, you will inevitably encounter two names: Preeti and Mangal. While they might look similar when printed on a piece of paper, the underlying technology powering these two fonts is completely different.

What is Preeti Font?

Preeti is a Legacy ASCII Font. It was created in the early days of computing before universal standards existed. To make the computer display Nepali characters, the creators of Preeti essentially "hacked" the English alphabet. For example, when you press the A key, the computer thinks you typed 'A', but the font draws a ब on the screen.

Pros: Excellent for offline Desktop Publishing (Adobe InDesign, PageMaker) because it avoids complex rendering bugs.
Cons: Text cannot be searched, pasted into Facebook, or read on mobile phones unless the other person also has the font installed.

What is Mangal Font?

Mangal is a TrueType Unicode Font developed by Microsoft. It is the default Devanagari font shipped with every copy of Windows. Unlike Preeti, Mangal uses the universal Unicode standard. When you type in Mangal, the computer explicitly knows you are typing a specific Devanagari character, not an English letter.

Pros: 100% web-safe. Text can be searched on Google, sent via email, and viewed perfectly on any smartphone worldwide without installing anything.
Cons: Cannot be used directly with legacy touch-typing layouts without a dedicated keyboard driver.

How to Convert Between Them

Because they use fundamentally different encoding systems, you cannot simply highlight text written in Preeti and change the font dropdown to Mangal. The text will turn into English gibberish. To switch fonts, you must translate the underlying code using our Preeti to Unicode Converter. Once converted to Unicode, you can safely apply the Mangal font to your text!

To use Excel correctly, you must input your data using Nepali Unicode (such as the Mangal font). Because Unicode assigns a unique digital code to every Devanagari character, Excel perfectly understands how to sort, filter, and search your data.

title: English to Nepali Translation: Accuracy and Best Practices
excerpt: Learn the difference between phonetic transliteration and actual translation, and discover the best tools for translating English to Nepali accurately.
content:
Translation vs. Transliteration

Many users confuse translation with transliteration. If you are typing "namaste" on your keyboard and the screen outputs "नमस्ते", that is transliteration (or phonetic typing). It simply changes the script from English letters to Devanagari.

However, English to Nepali translation means taking an English sentence like "How are you?" and converting its meaning into Nepali: "तपाईलाई कस्तो छ?".

Challenges in Nepali Translation

Translating between English and Nepali is notoriously difficult for AI and automated tools because the grammatical structures are entirely different. English follows a Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) order, while Nepali strictly follows a Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order.

  • English: I (Subject) eat (Verb) rice (Object).
  • Nepali: Ma (Subject) bhat (Object) khanchhu (Verb). -> म भात खान्छु।

Best Practices for Online Translation

When using online translation tools, follow these best practices to ensure the highest accuracy:

  1. Keep sentences short: Avoid long, complex paragraphs with multiple clauses. Break them down into simple sentences.
  2. Avoid idioms: English idioms like "It's raining cats and dogs" will translate literally into Nepali and confuse the reader. Say "It is raining heavily" instead.
  3. Check for formal tone: Nepali has multiple levels of respect (Timi vs. Tapai). Automated tools often default to "Timi" (informal). If you are translating a formal document, always manually review the text to ensure "Tapai" or "Hajur" is used appropriately.

title: How to Master the Preeti Keyboard Layout (With Cheat Sheet)
excerpt: Master the traditional Preeti keyboard layout with our comprehensive guide, tips for touch typing, and character cheat sheet.
content:
Why Learn the Preeti Keyboard Layout?

In the modern era of Romanized Unicode typing (where typing "k-a" gives you "क"), learning the traditional Preeti keyboard layout might seem outdated. However, it remains an absolutely essential skill in Nepal.

The Preeti layout is the industry standard for government offices, Lok Sewa Aayog examinations, journalism, and the traditional print media industry in Nepal. If you want a job in the Nepali public sector, mastering this layout is mandatory.

How the Layout Works

Unlike phonetic typing, the Preeti layout maps Devanagari characters directly to specific English keys, regardless of their sound. For example:

  • Pressing U types ग
  • Pressing O types इ
  • Pressing I types छ

Because there are more Devanagari characters (consonants and vowels) than there are keys on an English keyboard, you must frequently use the Shift key to access the other half of the alphabet. For instance, lowercase v types ख, but uppercase V (Shift + v) types खा (half-Kha).

Tips for Touch Typing in Preeti

  1. Start with the Home Row: Place your fingers on ASDF and JKL;. Memorize these keys first before moving to the top or bottom rows.
  2. Practice Half-Letters: Unlike Unicode which uses a halant to join letters automatically, Preeti requires you to memorize the specific keys for half-letters (often accessed via the Shift key).
  3. Use Typeshala: The classic Typeshala software is still the best way to build muscle memory for the Preeti layout.
